questions.q: Why does Meridian ERP integration use two different styles for order creation versus product/inventory sync?
options: Because order creation needs an immediate confirmed/rejected response, while inventory levels don't need second-by-second accuracy, so batch is cheaper and more predictable
Because Meridian cannot support any batch processing at all
Because Salesforce does not allow synchronous callouts to on-premises systems
Because product sync is handled entirely by LedgerPoint instead of Meridian
questions.explain: Order creation is synchronous because a rep or dealer needs to know right away whether the order succeeded; inventory sync runs as a cheaper, predictable nightly batch because that freshness isn't operationally necessary.

questions.q: What makes the Meridian order-creation callout idempotent?
options: It never retries under any circumstances
It uses Named Credentials instead of a username and password
It includes an order-reference ID that Meridian checks before processing, so a retried submission doesn't create a duplicate order
It is routed through Change Data Capture rather than a direct callout
questions.explain: Idempotency here comes specifically from an order-reference ID Meridian checks before processing — a retry after a network timeout resubmits the same reference rather than creating a second order.

questions.q: What does the LedgerPoint integration update on the Account record, per this lesson and Lesson 8's ownership map?
options: The full general ledger line detail, fully replicated
Summarized AR/invoice-status fields only, never full ledger detail
Nothing — LedgerPoint data never appears on the Account record
Only the dealer's financing terms
questions.explain: Consistent with Lesson 8's ownership map, only summarized AR/invoice-status fields are updated on the Account from the LedgerPoint batch — full ledger detail stays owned by LedgerPoint alone.

questions.q: Why does this lesson insist that LedgerPoint's batch-only integration is 'the correct design, not a compromise'?
options: Because batch integration is always superior to real-time integration in every scenario
Because Meridian's integration proves real-time is never necessary
Because the CFO personally prefers batch processing

Because LedgerPoint has no API at all, and modernizing it is outside this transformation's scope — so nightly batch with reconciliation, engineered deliberately, is the right answer given that fixed constraint
questions.explain: Given LedgerPoint's fixed no-API constraint, a carefully engineered batch-with-reconciliation design is the correct answer, not a lesser substitute for a 'real' real-time integration that was never achievable in this project's scope.

questions.q: What does the reconciliation step after each LedgerPoint batch cycle specifically catch?
options: Dropped or malformed records in the file transfer, by comparing record counts and key totals between what was sent and what was acknowledged
Performance issues in the Salesforce user interface
Governor limit violations in Apex triggers
Unauthorized access attempts to the Account object
questions.explain: Reconciliation compares counts and totals between the sent and acknowledged sides of the batch transfer specifically to catch silently dropped or malformed records quickly, rather than discovering the problem weeks later via a customer dispute.
